W03-DA06-S003-resources-1.claim: Invoice webhooks synchronously replay the affiliate's entire pending-transfer backlog before acknowledging delivery.
W03-DA06-S003-resources-1.failure_scenario: An affiliate with a connected Stripe account has 100 pending commissions after an outage. A valid invoice.payment_succeeded callback arrives while transfer requests stall until their 25-second timeout. The callback attempts all 100 transfers sequentially, including after individual failures, and cannot acknowledge delivery for roughly 2,500 seconds. Throughout replay it retains a database transaction and affiliate advisory lock; concurrent callbacks for that affiliate can occupy additional pool connections waiting for the lock. Duplicate delivery enters the same backlog replay again.
W03-DA06-S003-resources-1.evidence: billing_webhook.rs:174-194 returns the HTTP response only after process_event completes; :280-307 awaits process_commission even for duplicate billing events. affiliate_commission.rs:237-241 and :423 replay pending commissions for the whole affiliate. :476-492 holds one transaction and advisory lock throughout replay; :502-531 fetches every matching pending/failed commission without LIMIT and awaits each transfer. :593-615 records transfer failures as pending and returns Ok, so replay continues. stripe/client.rs:17,65-66 bounds each individual request to 25 seconds, not the complete webhook. Supporting sources were verified unchanged against review SHA 0ecae1370f1a80d1a101249b5c932663d69be8af.
W03-DA06-S003-resources-1.expected_behavior: The webhook's post-commit followups are described as best-effort operations intended to avoid Stripe retries (billing_webhook.rs:242-265), but acknowledgment here depends on an arbitrarily large backlog. A bounded acknowledgment/resource budget is needed while retaining durable, idempotent transfer recovery. No exact budget or batching/scheduling contract is established, and replaying all pending commissions is explicitly documented, so this is C rather than an automatic behavior-changing fix.
W03-DA06-S003-resources-1.countermeasures: Signature verification restricts entry to valid callbacks. Event uniqueness, commission uniqueness and Stripe idempotency keys prevent duplicate financial effects, but do not bound replay work. The 25-second Stripe timeout applies separately to every transfer. The pending-sum cap at affiliate_commission.rs:351-370 applies only without a connected account, so it does not constrain this scenario. The duplicate-recovery test at billing_webhook.rs:869-934 intentionally requires transfer recovery on replay. No aggregate request deadline appears in the inspected router/server layers; the exact desired execution policy therefore needs a design decision.
